page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration within the general-purpose N4 machine series. It provides 8 virtual CPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores on an Intel x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled. The processor architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Modern vector and matrix instruction extensions are supported, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing a compute-heavy memory-to-core density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or bundled GPUs, necessitating external network-attached block storage for persistence. The instance also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations place general processor performance solidly in the mid-tier, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 1877.0 and a multi-core score of 7215.0, matched by a PassMark CPU score of 12045.57. However, PassMark memory performance measures in the bottom quartile at 1718.22, with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth peaking at 68.85 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 40.33 GB/sec.

The 2:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation delivers cost-efficient compute capacity for workloads that demand dedicated processor cycles without large memory footprints. Performance bottlenecks can arise in memory-intensive processing or generative AI tasks with larger language models, where medium-sized 7B parameter text generation is constrained to 7.92 tokens per second. The instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD code compilation (demonstrated by a Clang score of 8701.0), distributed microservices, static web serving throughput, and mid-scale web application infrastructure.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused instance featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on modern Intel hardware, the processor supports AVX-512 and AMX extensions, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. The machine comes without bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on network storage for operational workloads. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates balanced mid-tier compute output, registering 1877.0 in Geekbench single-core and 7215.0 in multi-core metrics, with 11.89 GB/sec static web serving throughput. PassMark memory testing registers in the lower quartile, highlighting a resource configuration optimized for CPU-heavy tasks rather than large memory footprints. The profile makes this instance appropriate for CI/CD compilation, batch compute routines, compression pipelines, and distributed application microservices.
